question: Which of the following statements best reflects Sir Thomas Roe's famous advice to the East India Company's directors regarding their commercial strategy in India?
options: 'Assail the Portuguese on land, for their naval power is unmatched but their garrisons are weak.'
'Seek no territory, for war and traffic are incompatible; seek profit at sea and avoid costly fortifications.'
'Bribe the local subahdars rather than sending embassies to the Mughal Emperor, for the Emperor has no real power.'
'Establish factories only in the Deccan, for the Mughal Empire is on the verge of collapse.'
explanation: Sir Thomas Roe advised the Company: 'It is the folly of the Portuguese to agree to garrison and land wars... War and traffic are incompatible. If you will seek profit at sea, and avoid costly fortifications, you will prosper.' This piece of advice shaped EIC strategy for much of the 17th century.
